name: Ink Wash Painting
visualIdentity: Supplemental design reference, not a style directly named in the source collection. Uses pressure-sensitive brush marks, diluted washes, deliberate empty space and restrained tonal contrast. Choose one specific tradition and preserve its composition; Chinese ink wash and Japanese sumi-e are related but distinct.
suitableUses: Explicit good fits include product or editorial introductions, explanatory and illustrated narratives, and abstract or cinematic sequences with meaningful chapters. For video or interactive HTML, suitability is inferred from the style guidance; preserve space for observation and reading.
limitations: Usually works best alone. Avoid generic splashes, crowded compositions, added colors, and mixing Chinese inscriptions with sumi-e. Omit or adapt chapter transitions when the topic is too short, transitions obscure causality, or a cut conflicts with a continuous shot or loop. Interactive motion should respect reduced-motion needs.
palette: Optional suggestion for new art only: warm paper #F4EFDF background and ink #242724 foreground. Keep this pair monochrome; use opacity, hatching or patterns for tone, with gradients disabled. Task, brand and approved palettes and their role assignments take precedence; do not recolor source artwork or add accent hues. Recheck contrast on composited frames; two-color ratios do not guarantee readability over textures or images.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal strokes and washes coherently, preserving stroke direction and pigment layering. Use restrained movement and reading holds. Optional chapter handoffs or narrative steps can coordinate copy and imagery: scroll progress for interactive HTML, composition time for video. Support backward and direct seeks; keep transitions style-compatible and state coherent. Slow 2–3 wash-plane drift is suggested only for ambient scenes.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and explicit audio requirements; do not assume instrumental music or available assets. For chaptered storytelling, any accents or synchronization should support comprehension and leave space for speech.
assetRequirements: Use authentic ink assets or controlled brush and wash masks. Keep local fonts and assets loaded, and prepare or cache stateful simulations. Suggested supporting tools include Canvas 2D for deterministic brush, texture and bitmap drawing, and Python with Pillow for preprocessing, masks and compositing. These are role-based options, not mandatory bundle items.
combinations: Usually use ink wash alone. Optional Chinese ink calligraphy (style-041) can add a verified inscription for cultural or poetic pieces, with translation and verified wording; avoid mixing it with sumi-e. Optional restrained depth (style-101) can separate mountain and mist washes for meditative scenes, using opacity only, minimal slow movement and preserved empty space.
productionApproach: Select visual renderer and motion method for fidelity first; keep composition/export separate. HyperFrames is primary for scene assembly, seekable timing, media/audio sync, validation and export. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation prevents a required capability, and record why; an existing React project alone is insufficient. Drive video state from shared seekable time, seed randomness, and keep one owner per animated property. For interactive HTML, map finite scroll to coherent narrative states and provide readable static or reduced-motion behavior.
